summary: Wave A is mail and only what mail needs: the 07:00 text with the school lines first, 'did I get an email about X?', and the few switches, checks and one printed sheet that make it safe to leave running. Wave B is the rest of the reading Tony named or his roadmap planned next: public web pages, photos and PDFs he sends, outing plans, and calendar questions if the family calendar turns out to be on Google. Wave C is the first time Happy writes or sends anything: notes that last, then timed reminders and 'email me this', the last two only on Tony's yes. That places 17 of the 42 items; the other 25 are on the 'not in a wave yet' list, because nobody on record asked for them or they rest on a family fact nobody has confirmed, and because three plans of about 20 hours cannot honestly hold more.

plan_size.basis: M0 was 50 steps and M1 was 49 steps in nine phases whose own estimates add up to about 20 hours (about 25 minutes a step), and the roadmap budgets 8 to 10 hours a week and two weeks per milestone; this is an estimate, not a measurement.

waves.name: Happy reads your mail
waves.goal: Every weekday at 07:00 Tony gets one text of the mail that matters, school lines first, and can ask 'did I get an email about X?'; Jordan gets the same from her own inbox once she approves it herself.

phases.name: Prepare, and a Google sign-in that lasts
also_built_here: Tony's answers written down: Q8 part 1, Q11, Q5 and Q7
The change from the roadmap's 'mail on a local model only' rule recorded in the roadmap's decision table as Tony's own choice
The firewall (LuLu) installed and set to deny by default, with a rule that lets the mail connector reach Google and nothing else: the roadmap's gate before mail, in its cheapest form
A Google project with a sign-in app published to 'In production'
gog installed from the admin account, with its options confirmed from its own help output (the cards read them from the web only)
Tony's read-only, Gmail-only sign-in, approved by Tony on Google's consent screen
phases.goes_live_when: Nothing is switched on in this phase. It is done when one mail search run by hand works with a token that can read and cannot change anything, the firewall shows the connector talking to Google only, and the day-1 date is written down for the day-8 half of T1.

phases.name: Scheduler safety
also_built_here: Three scheduler switches: failed-job alerts go to Tony, runs missed during a power cut are skipped, script triggers are off

One short checked-in script that creates each job with the owner's handle read from the family file, a time limit and a tool list on every job (S9); as designed this is a generator that compares and removes jobs and writes a charter per job, about 2.5 hours more
phases.goes_live_when: The deploy path can list every job, a throwaway job added twice shows whether it updates or doubles, and a job made to fail alerts Tony and nobody else.

phases.name: The mail agent, kept apart
also_built_here: One locked-down mail agent per connected inbox, generated from the family file, pinned to one model with no fallback, holding only the Gmail read tools
Its own capped model key, as every agent has
The connector denied by name on every other agent
The separation check and the 'read the other parent's mail' canary extended to the connector

Only if Tony wants two layers before mail: the roadmap's coded check on which agent may call an account connector, built after T5 (about 3 hours more; otherwise it arrives with the blocking check in wave C)
phases.goes_live_when: Each agent's tool list shows the Gmail read tools on the mail agent and nowhere else, a test copy of another agent asked to read Tony's mail gets nothing, and the mail agent has no web, file, code, browser, draft or send tool.

phases.name: The 07:00 text, school lines first
also_built_here: G015's morning digest: one weekday job per connected inbox, delivered only to that inbox's owner
Planted test mails: one that carries instructions, one with a false deadline, one with a medical subject
The first week of real texts read by Tony before any school system's settings are touched
phases.goes_live_when: On a run started by hand, a planted mail that carries instructions produces nothing but its own line in the text to Tony: no tool is called except reading mail, nothing is sent to anyone else, and the firewall shows only the connector talking to Google. Then the 07:00 job is switched on for Tony's inbox.

phases.name: 'Did I get an email about X?'
also_built_here: G015's lookup: Tony's own agent may hand a mail question to his own mail agent and to no other agent
A planted mail that tells the reader to make Tony's agent do something
phases.goes_live_when: The hand-off returns its answer in the same chat while agents still cannot see each other's sessions (T4's check, here from Tony's agent to his mail agent), and the planted mail causes no tool call by Tony's agent. This is the part to drop first if the plan runs long.

phases.name: Keeping it sound, and one printed sheet
also_built_here: One daily check that each Google sign-in is still valid, reporting to Tony the way his existing checks do (S14); the audits and the restore drill stay commands Tony runs on the roadmap's schedule

One printed sheet for both parents: what the morning text is, the built-in stop and status commands (they work for Tony only), what an error reply means, and how to tell that Happy is down and that nothing is broken
phases.goes_live_when: A sign-in broken on purpose is reported to Tony within a day, and the sheet's wording matches what the five test texts and one provoked failure actually returned.

phases.name: Jordan's inbox
also_built_here: Jordan's own read-only sign-in, approved by her on Google's screen
Her mail agent, her 07:00 job and her canary, generated from the same family-file entry
phases.goes_live_when: Only if Q7 is answered yes. Her mail agent passes the same checks as Tony's, and neither parent's agents can read the other's mail.

phases.name: Exit gate
also_built_here: The day-8 mail search, the second half of T1
Deep security audit, separation check and canaries run again
Sign-off written in the config repo
phases.goes_live_when: The exit test passes; if the day-8 search fails, the choice between a weekly sign-in and a different connector goes back to Tony before the wave is called done.

new_risks: Private mail, which is also outside content, is read by an agent and sent to the cloud model (the roadmap planned a local model for mail). This is the one new kind of risk in this wave.

Two further steps of the same kind, each switched on in its own phase after its own test: the first job that runs unattended on a schedule, and mail answers relayed into the agent that holds a parent's chat memory (the lookup, which goes one step beyond the roadmap's mail design).
waves.exit_test: On a weekday at 07:00 Tony's phone gets one text built from his real inbox with the school lines first, while a planted mail that carries instructions causes nothing except its own line in that text, a test copy of Jordan's agent asked to read Tony's mail gets nothing, and the read-only sign-in still works on day 8 or later.

estimate.basis: Estimate. I listed the steps the way M1 did and counted 39 at about 30 minutes each: sign-in and firewall 3.5 h, scheduler 1.5 h, mail agent 3.5 h, morning text 3 h, lookup 2 h, check and sheet 2 h, Jordan 1.5 h, exit gate 2.5 h. Built as the cards are written it grows by about 20 hours and to about 75 steps: a job generator with charters (2.5 h), a separate afternoon school job with a sender list and a coded search check that needs the blocking plugin (6.5 h), a tax-form job and a second model tool (1.5 h), the full self-check card (3 h), the stop plugin (4 h), the outage script (2 h), the envelope and rehearsal (1.5 h). With the coded connector check added to the simplified form it is about 22.5 hours and 44 steps, still one plan.

needs_from_tony: Q8 part 1: may real mail text go to the cloud model before OpenAI answers on Zero Data Retention. Without a yes the wave can be built and tested but not switched on, so it cannot finish.

Q11, the mail half: that the firewall rule and the planted-mail test stand in for the roadmap's 'the reader makes no network calls', and whether the coded connector check comes before mail (3 hours more) or with wave C.
Q5: one mail text a day or two, and at what time (default: one, weekdays at 07:00).
Q7: whether Jordan wants the text and will approve her own inbox on Google's screen.
A yes or no on S6, S9 and S14: without them this wave is about 40 hours, which is two plans.
Q9 and Q12, only if Tony wants more than the printed sheet: a stop phrase for Jordan, or an envelope so she can restart Happy.
Q2 part 3 (which school systems send mail), only if S6 is not taken.
relies_on_simplifications: S6: one morning text with a school section, instead of two jobs per parent, a sender list, a search check, a tax-form job and a second model tool. The wave cannot fit without this one (about 8 hours).
S9: three scheduler switches and one short script, instead of a generator with a charter per job (2.5 hours). It can be declined on its own and the wave still fits.

S14: one daily sign-in check and a few lines on paper, instead of the full self-check card, the outage script and the envelope (about 6.5 hours). The outage script could not be in this wave in any case, because it needs family delivery (G009), which is not in a wave.

conditional_items.condition: The 07:00 text for Tony's inbox is not conditional. Jordan's inbox and her copy of the text are built only if Q7 is answered yes and she approves on Google's screen herself. The lookup goes live only after its own planted-mail test.

As designed (its own afternoon text held to a school sender list) only if Q2 part 3 names the school systems and Q5 asks for a second text; otherwise it ships as the school lines at the top of the 07:00 text (S6).

In this wave as the printed sheet of built-in commands. The in-house 'stop everything' phrase and the lock-out are built only if Q9 is answered that Jordan needs her own stop, and then in wave C on the one blocking check.
In this wave only as one line on the printed sheet (S14). The outage-notice script is in no wave: it needs family delivery (G009).
In this wave as the half page that tells Jordan how to recognise that Happy is down. The envelope and restart steps only if Q12 says she should bring Happy back herself and T10 passes.

waves.name: Happy reads the web and what you send it
waves.goal: A parent can ask Happy something that needs a public web page and get the answer with its link and the time it was fetched, send a photo or PDF and ask about it, ask for a plan for Saturday, and, if the family calendar is on Google, ask what is on.

phases.name: Prepare, and the gate before web reading
also_built_here: Tony's answers written down: Q11 (the outbound proxy), Q13, Q8 part 2 and Q4

The roadmap's gate before the first web-reading agent, in the form Tony picks: the outbound proxy (Smokescreen) installed, run in report mode and then enforcing, or his written waiver for the plain page-fetch tool
A firewall rule for the gateway's own page fetches
The roadmap's Prompt Guard tripwire either built or waived in writing; it needs a small local classifier and no local model is installed
phases.goes_live_when: Nothing is switched on in this phase. It is done when the proxy is enforcing and a blocked address is refused while model calls still work, or when Tony's waiver is written into the roadmap's decision table.

phases.name: The web helper
also_built_here: A shared research agent with no memory, no accounts and a fresh sandbox per session, with its own capped model key
Each parent's agent may hand tasks to it and to no other shared agent
Test cases: a home-network address, a public link that redirects to one, a public name that resolves to one, and a search result that asks the parent's agent to pass its notes to the helper
Wave A's planted-mail lookup case run again now that the helper exists
phases.goes_live_when: T4 passes first: the helper's answer comes back in the same chat with sessions still private. Then the four test cases and the mail case run again cause no fetch of a private address and no hand-off that carries memory.

phases.name: Photos and PDFs you send
also_built_here: One setting switches attachment reading on; audio understanding stays off
One line on the printed sheet: no bank, tax or medical papers (S7); as designed, a privacy-gate plugin for text PDFs is built and proven first, about 2.5 hours more
A PDF with hidden instructions as a test case
phases.goes_live_when: Q8 part 2 is answered yes, and the PDF with hidden instructions causes no tool call, a hand-off to the web helper counted as one.

phases.name: Calendar questions
also_built_here: A calendar-only, read-only Google sign-in per parent, stored apart from the mail sign-in (wave A's published sign-in app is reused)
An event title that carries instructions as a test case
phases.goes_live_when: Only if Q4 says the shared family calendar is on Google. The calendar sign-in cannot run a mail search (the second half of T2), each parent's agent shows one calendar tool and only its own, and the planted event title causes no tool call.

phases.name: Outings, with the hourly forecast
also_built_here: The weather tool follows the hourly forecast (hourly only, S15)
Planner rules on the web helper: two options with opening hours, the weather and links; a price only from a page it read; links, not bookings
Test cases for constraints met and for prices that come from a fetched page
phases.goes_live_when: 'Will it rain at home on Saturday between 9 and noon?' gets an hour-by-hour answer, and a plan request returns options whose hours, prices and links all trace to pages the helper fetched, with nothing booked.

phases.name: Exit gate
also_built_here: Deep security audit, separation check and canaries run again
The printed sheet reprinted with the new lines
Sign-off written in the config repo

new_risks: An agent that reads the open web, with a hand-off from the agent that holds a parent's chat memory. The roadmap names that hand-off as its one remaining leak path.

Outside content read directly by the agent that holds a parent's memory: photos and PDFs, and calendar text if the calendar phase is built. Family photos and PDFs also go to the cloud model. This is a second kind of risk, so it is switched on in its own phases, after the web helper has passed its tests and after its own.
waves.exit_test: Tony asks a question that needs a public page and gets the answer with its link and the time fetched; in the same run a page that points at a home-network address, a search result that asks his agent to pass its notes to the web helper, and a PDF with hidden instructions cause no fetch of a private address, no hand-off that carries memory and no other tool call.

estimate.basis: Estimate. 34 steps at about 30 minutes: gate with the proxy built 4 h, web helper 3.75 h, photos and PDFs 2 h, calendar 3 h, outings 2.5 h, exit gate 2.5 h. If Tony waives the proxy it is about 15 hours; without the calendar phase about 3 hours less again. Built as the cards are written it is about 27 hours and about 58 steps: the outing planner alone is rated large (about 7 h with a paid Google place lookup, a Friday text and a passport line), the privacy-gate plugin adds 2.5 h and the web helper's scripted 'on it' and 'cancel that' about 1 h.

needs_from_tony: Q11, the web half: build the outbound proxy before web reading, as the roadmap says, or waive it in writing for the plain page-fetch tool. With no answer the roadmap stands and the proxy is built first.
Q13: what Happy may put into a web search or hand to the web helper (default: town and ages yes, names and school no).
Q8 part 2: may photos and PDFs a parent chooses to send go to the cloud model before OpenAI answers on Zero Data Retention.
Q4: where the family keeps its events. The calendar phase is built only if the answer is a Google calendar.
A yes or no on S13 for the outing planner; S7 and S15 make the wave smaller but it fits without them.
relies_on_simplifications: S13, the part about F028: the outing planner runs on the web helper alone, without the paid Google place lookup, the Friday text and the passport line. As designed that one card is about 7 hours, takes the wave to about 27, and leans on two cards that are not in this wave (emailed plans, the renewals table).

conditional_items.condition: Only if Q4 is answered that the shared family calendar is a Google calendar; Jordan's calendar sign-in only if she approves it herself (Q7).
Switched on only if Q8 part 2 is answered yes or OpenAI approves Zero Data Retention; if neither, this phase is skipped and the wave ends without it.

waves.name: Happy remembers, reminds and emails you
waves.goal: A parent can say 'remember this' and find it again next week, and, on Tony's yes, 'remind me at 4:30' arrives as a text, a flyer's dates become reminders after a yes, and 'email me this' lands in the asker's own inbox.

phases.name: Prepare, and the one blocking check
also_built_here: Tony's answers written down: Q6, Q9 part b, Q10 (keep chat excerpts or only what a parent asks for), Q2, and Q3 for 'email me this'
The roadmap's one in-house plugin: one blocking check that fails closed and a short rule table read from the family file, with no rule active yet
If it was not built in wave A: the roadmap's rule on which agent may call which account connector
phases.goes_live_when: T5 shows the check is called for file writes, the scheduling tool and the mail send tool, and which fields it is given; a check that throws blocks the call; and with no rule active Happy behaves as before.

phases.name: Notes that last, and the family facts
also_built_here: Keyword-only note search set explicitly, so no note text goes to a cloud embedding service
The rule that limits where Happy may write, only if T6 shows the closed-sandbox route does not work
A generator step that renders the facts Tony types into the family file into each parent's own agent, and into no shared or mail agent
phases.goes_live_when: For each parent: a note is saved, a new chat finds it, it survives a sandbox rebuild and is in the nightly backup; a long chat saves nothing by itself; a write outside the notes is refused; the family facts still load; and a test copy of the other parent's agent cannot get the note.

phases.name: Timed reminders, and dates from a flyer
also_built_here: The first rule in the blocking check: a reminder may only be a text to the person who asked, with no web address and no tools; changing or running a job from chat is refused
The scheduling tool allowed on Tony's own agent only (Jordan is not a command owner)
A standing order: after reading a flyer Happy lists the dates in full and sets reminders only after a yes (S11); no calendar write
phases.goes_live_when: Only if Q6 is answered yes. T7 passes first. Then seeded tries to aim a reminder at another person, at a web address, or with tools attached are all blocked, and a flyer with hidden instructions creates no reminder without a yes.

phases.name: Email me this
also_built_here: A send-only sign-in for the sending address (wave A's published sign-in app is reused)
A mail-out server that registers only the send tool, allowed to each parent's own agent and to no shared or mail agent
The second rule in the blocking check: the only recipient is the owner of the agent that sends; no cc, bcc, reply-all, alias or HTML
The emailed long version of an outing plan from wave B comes with this, at no extra build
phases.goes_live_when: Only if Tony says yes to this item under Q3. Five seeded ways to change the recipient, another family member and a reply-all among them, are all blocked; an injected web page cannot change the recipient; and the send is blocked when the check itself fails.

phases.name: Exit gate
also_built_here: Deep security audit, separation check and canaries run again
One smoke case each for notes, reminders and email added to the existing eval set
The printed sheet reprinted; sign-off written in the config repo

new_risks: Happy writes or sends something for the first time. The wave adds this in three forms, each switched on in its own phase behind the same blocking check and after its own test.
Notes that persist: a saved note is where a planted instruction could stay.
The scheduling tool on the agent that holds a parent's memory: without the rule it could name where a job's output goes.
Email that leaves iMessage: the first output that is not a chat reply.
waves.exit_test: Tony saves a note, starts a new chat the next day and gets it back; sets a reminder that arrives on time and reaches only him; and seeded tries to write outside the notes, to aim a reminder at another person or a web address, and (if email is built) to send to any address but his own are all blocked by the one check, which also blocks when it fails.

estimate.basis: Estimate, with every conditional item answered yes. 36 steps at about 30 minutes: blocking check 2.5 h, notes and family facts 4.5 h, reminders and flyer dates 4.5 h, email 4.5 h, exit gate 2.5 h, and about half an hour of slack if T6 fails and the write rule is needed. Without email it is about 14.5 hours; without reminders about 4.5 hours less again. Built as the cards are written it is about 30 hours: the calendar-write server for flyer dates (5 h), the family-delivery card's check that reminders name as a prerequisite (2 h), the fuller notes design with chat excerpts and web-call tracking (1.5 h), family facts rendered into the memory file with a reply-language line (1.5 h), and a send cap and a new sender account (1 h).

A yes or no on S11 and S5: without them this wave is about 30 hours and one of its items waits on a card that is in no wave.

S5: the reminder check is built with reminders, and texts from one parent's Happy into the other's chat stay off, as the roadmap has them. As designed the check belongs to the family-delivery card (G009), which is not in a wave.

notes: Honest size. Built exactly as the cards are written today, none of the three waves is one plan: A is about 40 hours, B about 27 and C about 30. Each fits only with the simplifications named on it: S6 (and S9 or S14) for A, S13 for B, S11 and S5 for C. Tony has confirmed none of these yet, so the first thing each plan needs is a yes or no on them.

The three waves together are about 57 hours, about six weeks at 8 to 10 hours a week, and they hold 17 of the 42 items. A design that starts from what Tony asked for cannot hold more without building on things he has not said. If he wants more in A to C, the cheapest additions are named on the list: the handbook folder (F043, 1.5 h), one evening text (F014, 1.5 h) and the single deny line from MAC-04.

All hours are my estimates. The cards' S, M and L have no unit; I read them as about 1 to 2, 3 to 5 and 6 to 9 hours, checked against M1, where a phase of five or six steps took 2.5 to 3 hours. Almost nothing here has been tried live, so the hours cover the case where each first test passes. A failed T1 (the token dies after seven days), T4 (the hand-off does not return) or T6 changes the plan, and the plan should stop and ask Tony instead of absorbing it.

Wave A cannot finish without Tony's answer to Q8 part 1. If the answer is to wait for OpenAI, wave B does not depend on wave A except in its calendar phase, so B could run while A waits; wave C needs A's scheduler switches and sign-in app.

Three places where the waves leave the roadmap, each to be written into its decision table as Tony's choice before the plan starts: mail is read on the cloud model, so the roadmap's exit test 'the reader makes no network calls' is replaced by the firewall rule and the planted-mail test; the lookup brings mail answers into the parent's own agent, one step beyond the roadmap's mail design; and the roadmap's gates for web reading and mail also name tracing and retention levels (O2, O3) that were never built because the local-model milestone was skipped. Those are not in my hours; building tracing first would add about 3 hours to wave A.

Until wave C there is one layer, not two, between a parent's agent and the other parent's mail: tool permissions with an explicit deny, proven by two tests. The roadmap's second layer, a coded check, comes with the blocking check in wave C unless Tony asks for it in wave A (3 hours more; A still fits).

Hard rules checked per wave. A: the mail agent holds private mail and reads outside content but has no way out except its scheduled text to its owner. B: the web helper reads the open web but holds no memory, no accounts and no family data; the parent's own agent still cannot browse. C: every write or send is pinned in code that fails closed, to the asker alone, which is stricter than 'the family'. No wave adds a payment, a booking, a browser that types, a group chat or a send into another person's conversation.

What moved from the old wave A of 19: web reading, photos and PDFs, the calendar and the weather upgrade go to B; notes, family facts and reminders go to C; the jobs card, the self-checks and the three paper cards stay in A in their small forms; voice, the group chat, family delivery, the Reminders bridge, the household database, the handbook and the device deny list are not in a wave.

Three cards are in wave A only on paper (G005, CRT-04, CRT-05). If Tony wants them as designed (a stop plugin, an outage script, an envelope with a rehearsal) they add about 8 hours and leave wave A; the stop plugin would then sit on wave C's blocking check, and the outage script would wait for family delivery.

If Tony answers no to both reminders (Q6) and 'email me this' (Q3), wave C is notes and family facts alone, about 10 hours. The handbook folder and, if the calendar is on Google, the evening text are the natural things to fill it with, each on his yes.
